**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY)** — submitted.

**What I reviewed:** §§ 19.1–19.5 (warranties, remedy, disclaimer), § 6.1–6.2 (acceptance), and the definition of "Deliverable."

**Assessment:**
- Most of the warranty package already sits at or above the preferred position: § 19.1 (professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, material conformity to documentation and specifications), § 19.3 (no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, open-source protection), § 19.4 (re-perform/repair/replace, then terminate and refund Fees paid — plus non-exclusivity carve-outs), and § 19.5 (disclaimer expressly does not swallow express warranties).
- The one material failure is **duration**: § 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformity warranty at **fifteen days** after delivery and then says Vendor has "no correction or refund obligation." That is below the fallback (30/90 days) and, worse, it overrides the open-ended § 19.1 conformity warranty and shuts off the § 19.4 remedy for Deliverables. Because § 6.1 gives us fifteen *business* days just to test, the warranty would expire at or before acceptance.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** § 19.2 — "fifteen days" → "ninety days," and the cut-off sentence replaced with confirmation that § 19.2 does not limit § 19.1 or § 19.4. This is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position while leaving the rest of the Article 19 bargain intact.
